description: The configuration surface of the clickhouse chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

clusterName.description: The name of the single ClickHouse cluster inside the installation.
clusterName.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: It reaches the tenant's SQL — ON CLUSTER and Distributed() name it — so it is a constant rather than a setting: changing it would break DDL the platform cannot see. It is here because the two templates both need it, not because anybody may set it.

imageName.description: Override the full ClickHouse server image reference, tag included. Empty means clickhouse/clickhouse-server:{version}.
imageName.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: A pinned reference defeats the version property, so it is a platform escape hatch rather than a tenant setting.

keeperImageName.description: Override the full ClickHouse Keeper image reference, tag included. Empty means clickhouse/clickhouse-keeper:{version}.
keeperImageName.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Keeper and server share a release train, so the version property tags both. Splitting them is a platform escape hatch for an upgrade window, not a tenant setting.

keeperNodes.description: Number of ClickHouse Keeper nodes. Keeper is a Raft quorum, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one and an even count tolerates no more failures than the odd count below it. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all.

enabled.description: Whether ClickHouse's own Prometheus endpoint is served on port 9363. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ It makes the metrics exist; the object that scrapes them is not built — see conformance.yaml § owed.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

replicas.description: Number of replicas per shard. This is the availability axis, and it only applies to tables the tenant creates as Replicated — the resource does not manage tables. Total server count is shards times replicas.

shards.description: Number of shards. This is the capacity and parallelism axis: a table's data is split across shards and a query fans out to all of them. ⚠ Resharding an existing table is not something the operator or this resource does, so growing this moves new data only.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per ClickHouse server, either by preset or explicitly. The Keeper nodes are sized by the platform and are not affected.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 8Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Analytics uses the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB.

storage.description: The data volume, per ClickHouse server.

class.description: StorageClass name for the ClickHouse servers and the Keeper nodes. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Data volume size per ClickHouse server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

version.description: ClickHouse version, which is also the ClickHouse Keeper version — the two share a release train and a wire protocol. Only long-term-support lines are offered; a new api-version is what adds a third.
